title: Trends and prospects in dairy protein replacement in yogurt and cheese

laymanSummary.question: What is the future outlook?
laymanSummary.answer: While plant-based options are common, they often fall short in functionality. Single-cell and recombinant proteins show immense promise for their high nutritional value and sustainable production potential. Although technical and sensory challenges remain, this research is critical for developing the next generation of healthy, sustainable, and enjoyable dairy-free foods.

laymanSummary.question: What are the main alternatives?
laymanSummary.answer: We review three main categories: plant-based proteins (from soy, peas, oats), single-cell proteins (from microbes like algae and yeast), and recombinant proteins (animal proteins produced by genetically engineered microbes). We examine the nutritional profiles, functional properties, and production methods for each.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: As global demand for protein grows, the environmental impact of traditional dairy is a major concern. This review explores the progress in creating sustainable alternatives to dairy proteins for use in popular products like yogurt and cheese, without sacrificing nutrition, texture, or taste.

title: BIORREACTOR MODULAR CON PARTES INTERCAMBIABLES
publicationVenue: Assignee: UNIVERSIDAD DE LOS ANDES, UNIVERSIDAD ANTONIO NARIÑO

laymanSummary.question: What is the innovative solution?
laymanSummary.answer: This patent presents a modular bioreactor designed like a set of building blocks. Its key innovation is a versatile, tool-free connection system with specialized silicone seals that allows researchers to quickly and easily swap components, reconfiguring the same core unit for various experimental needs while ensuring a perfectly sterile environment.

laymanSummary.question: What was the problem?
laymanSummary.answer: Traditional laboratory bioreactors for growing cells or bacteria are expensive and inflexible. If a scientist needs a different setup for a new experiment, they often have to buy an entirely new machine, which is costly and inefficient.

laymanSummary.question: What is the practical application?
laymanSummary.answer: This invention provides a highly versatile and cost-effective platform for scientific research. A single unit can be adapted for multiple types of bioprocesses—such as a stirred-tank, packed-bed, or airlift reactor—significantly reducing equipment costs and lab space for researchers in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and biofuel development.

title: Tailoring Magnetite-Nanoparticle-Based Nanocarriers for Gene Delivery: Exploiting CRISPRa Potential in Reducing Conditions
Unlocking cellular barriers: silica nanoparticles and fullerenol conjugated cell-penetrating agents for enhanced intracellular drug delivery
publicationVenue: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology, Volume 11

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: All four delivery systems were effective at entering cells without causing harm. Crucially, we found that the type of nanoparticle carrier influenced the ultimate destination of the cargo within the cell. This demonstrates that by simply changing the support structure, we can tailor drug delivery systems for specific tasks, paving the way for more precise and effective therapies.

laymanSummary.question: What was our modular approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We took two known cell-penetrating agents (OmpA and Buforin II) and attached them to two different types of nanoparticle carriers (silica spheres and fullerenol). By creating and testing these four unique combinations, we investigated how the choice of carrier affects the performance of the delivery system.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Getting therapeutic drugs inside our cells is a major hurdle in medicine. This study aimed to build a robust and modular drug delivery system by combining different cell-penetrating agents with different nanoscopic support structures to see which combinations work best.

title: Breaking the clean room barrier: exploring low-cost alternatives for microfluidic devices
publicationVenue: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology, Volume 11

laymanSummary.question: What are the alternative solutions?
laymanSummary.answer: This review explores the growing ecosystem of low-cost alternatives that are democratizing microfluidics. We detail how affordable materials like polymers, paper, and hydrogels are replacing expensive silicon and glass, while accessible fabrication methods like soft lithography, laser cutting, and 3D printing are replacing complex clean room processes.

laymanSummary.question: Why is this shift important?
laymanSummary.answer: By breaking down the financial and technical barriers of the clean room, these low-cost alternatives are empowering more scientists to innovate. This will accelerate the development and integration of microfluidic technology into a wide range of applications, from point-of-care medical diagnostics to quality control in the food industry.

title: How does sound shape our smell perception beyond flavors? A review of experimental studies

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We conducted a systematic review of 10 experimental studies published between 2012 and 2022 that explored sound-smell associations outside the food industry. We analyzed their methodologies, the types of sounds and scents used, and the specific crossmodal connections they successfully validated.

laymanSummary.question: What are the key implications?
laymanSummary.answer: Our findings confirm that specific sound-aroma connections exist (e.g., bird sounds are associated with lilac, high-pitched tones with lemon). This review highlights a critical need for further research, especially for cosmetic and pharmaceutical products. The insights provide a foundation for designing multisensory experiences that can make products more appealing and effective, simply by leveraging the power of sound.

title: Insectopia: The Untapped Potential of Insects for a Healthier, Greener World

laymanSummary.question: What does the book cover?
laymanSummary.answer: This book serves as a comprehensive guide, covering the latest advancements in insect farming, production technologies, and the development of new, appealing food products. It also confronts the key cultural and psychological barriers to insect consumption and discusses practical strategies for overcoming them.

title: The Impact of Yeast Encapsulation in Wort Fermentation and Beer Flavor Profile

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We encapsulated four different yeast strains in alginate beads and conducted fermentations, comparing the resulting beers to those made with traditional free-floating yeast. We then analyzed their chemical composition, physical properties, and sensory profiles to measure the impact of encapsulation.

title: Design and Assembly of a Biofactory for (2S)-Naringenin Production in Escherichia coli: Effects of Oxygen Transfer on Yield and Gene Expression

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: We discovered that precisely controlling oxygen levels is crucial for maximizing yield. By optimizing this condition, we achieved a production titer of 3.11 g/L, one of the highest reported to date. Gene expression analysis confirmed that different oxygen levels activate distinct metabolic pathways, providing a clear roadmap for scaling up sustainable, industrial production of this valuable nutraceutical.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: (2S)-naringenin is a natural, health-promoting compound found in citrus, but traditional extraction methods are inefficient and unsustainable. While engineering bacteria like E. coli to produce it is a promising alternative, achieving high yields remains a significant hurdle.

title: Academia y sostenibilidad, un 'match' necesario

laymanSummary.question: What is the core argument?
laymanSummary.answer: Universities have a responsibility to actively integrate sustainability into their core mission through innovative educational models. We argue that this involves combining project-based learning with the transformation of university campuses into "living laboratories" for sustainable practices.

laymanSummary.question: What evidence is presented?
laymanSummary.answer: We propose three key strategies: 1) Using project-based learning to tackle real-world sustainability challenges like resource conservation and circular economy. 2) Converting campus infrastructure into an active testbed for sustainability in energy, waste, and water management. 3) Building interdisciplinary collaborations and partnerships with local communities and businesses.

laymanSummary.question: Why is this important?
laymanSummary.answer: This approach is vital for training a new generation of professionals and citizens equipped not just with theoretical knowledge, but with the practical skills and systemic thinking needed to lead the transition to a more sustainable and resilient future for everyone.

title: Novel Biosurfactants: Rationally Designed Surface-Active Peptides and in silico Evaluation at the Decane-Water Interface

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Most surfactants, which allow oil and water to mix, are derived from petrochemicals and harm the environment. This research aimed to design new, effective, and eco-friendly biosurfactants from the ground up using peptides (short protein chains).

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: Our simulations accurately predicted that the designed peptides would be effective surfactants, migrating to the oil-water interface and reducing tension. This study showcases a powerful and efficient computational method that can accelerate the discovery of next-generation, custom-designed biosurfactants, paving the way for more sustainable consumer and industrial products.

title: Modeling and Simulation of Magnetoliposome Formation by Encapsulation of Core-Shell, Magnetite-Chitosan Nanoparticles in Liposomes Enabled by a Low-Cost Microfluidic System

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our computer simulations showed high agreement with experimental results, demonstrating that our model can accurately predict encapsulation efficiency. This provides a powerful computational tool to accelerate the design of low-cost microfluidic systems for producing advanced nanomedicines, making targeted drug delivery more accessible.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We designed a low-cost microfluidic chip with various channel geometries to synthesize the magnetoliposomes. The process was modeled using advanced computer simulations (COMSOL Multiphysics) with a specific turbulence model (κ-ε model) to predict and optimize the encapsulation efficiency.

title: Estimation and prediction of the air-water interfacial tension in conventional and peptide surface-active agents by Random Forest Regression

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: The model demonstrated strong predictive power, accurately estimating surfactant performance and identifying clear design rules. It revealed that peptides rich in hydrophobic amino acids (like leucine and isoleucine) are the most effective. This research introduces a valuable AI tool that can significantly accelerate the discovery of sustainable, high-performance biosurfactants.

title: Smart Nanocarriers for Targeted Gene Therapy: A Magnetoliposome-Based Approach
publicationVenue: Annual Meeting of the Biomedical Engineering Society (BMES)

laymanSummary.question: What was demonstrated?
laymanSummary.answer: We presented data from our microfluidic fabrication system, which produces highly uniform magnetoliposomes with high encapsulation efficiency. Our in-vitro results showed successful, targeted delivery into cells, showcasing a promising platform for developing safer and more effective gene therapies.

title: Assessing cellular internalization and endosomal escape abilities of novel BUFII-Graphene oxide nanobioconjugates

laymanSummary.question: What was our innovative solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We engineered a novel nanocarrier by attaching a potent cell-penetrating peptide (Buforin II) to sheets of graphene oxide. We created two versions with different chemical linkers—one designed to be stable and another designed to break apart inside the cell—to test how linker chemistry affects performance.

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: Both nanocarriers were highly effective at entering cells and proved to be very biocompatible. Crucially, the nanocarrier with the breakable linker showed a high rate of endosomal escape (up to 45%) in certain cell types. This work provides critical insights for designing the next generation of smart drug delivery systems, demonstrating that linker chemistry can be tuned to overcome specific cellular barriers.

title: CRISPR/nCas9-Based Genome Editing on GM2 Gangliosidoses Fibroblasts via Non-Viral Vectors
publicationVenue: International Journal of Molecular Sciences, Volume 23, Issue 18, Pages 10672

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: GM2 gangliosidoses, a group of fatal genetic disorders including Tay-Sachs disease, cause devastating neurological damage with no available cure. Gene editing offers hope for a permanent correction, but safely delivering the necessary tools into patient cells remains a critical barrier.

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: The gene-editing therapy was highly successful. Corrected cells began producing the missing enzyme and showed significant recovery, with less waste accumulation and reduced cellular stress. This work validates the therapeutic potential of CRISPR-based strategies for these fatal diseases and introduces novel, safer delivery methods to advance the field of gene therapy.

laymanSummary.question: What was our innovative solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We developed a gene-editing therapy using a safer version of CRISPR (nCas9) to insert a correct copy of the defective gene. We tested two non-viral delivery methods: standard liposomes and a novel system using magnetic fatty bubbles (magnetoliposomes) to transport the genetic tools into cells from patients with Tay-Sachs and Sandhoff disease.

title: Delivery and assessment of a CRISPR/nCas9-based genome editing system on in vitro models of mucopolysaccharidoses IVA assisted by magnetite-based nanoparticles

laymanSummary.question: What was our innovative solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We used the CRISPR/nCas9 gene-editing tool to correct the defective gene in cells from MPS IVA patients. To deliver the tool, we developed a novel, non-viral vehicle made of tiny magnetic particles coated in a fatty layer (magnetoliposomes), which can safely transport the gene-editing machinery into cells.

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: The gene editing was highly successful. The treated cells showed a significant increase in enzyme activity and a reduction in harmful sugar buildup and cellular stress. Crucially, our magnetoliposome delivery system performed as effectively as standard methods, proving it is a safe and powerful new technology for advancing gene therapies for MPS IVA and other genetic disorders.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Mucopolysaccharidosis IVA (MPS IVA) is a debilitating genetic disorder affecting the skeleton. While enzyme replacement therapy exists, it is limited in its effectiveness. Gene therapy offers a potential cure, but safely delivering gene-editing tools into cells remains a major hurdle.

title: The Sounds of Freshness: Soundtracks that crossmodally correspond with sensations associated to olfactory freshness
publicationVenue: International Federation of Societies of Cosmetic Chemists Conference (IFSCC 2022), London

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: Our results confirmed a clear link between sound and scent. Specific sounds—particularly those with woodwind and piano instruments, low tempo, and legato articulation—were found to significantly enhance the perceived freshness of the perfume. This study provides evidence-based guidelines for using sound design to craft more immersive and appealing multisensory experiences for consumers.

title: Rational Discovery of Antimicrobial Peptides by Means of Artificial Intelligence

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We created a complete computational pipeline to accelerate discovery. The core is our novel deep learning model, AMPs-Net, which analyzes vast peptide libraries to predict antimicrobial activity. We combined this with molecular dynamics simulations to predict how the peptides interact with cell membranes before validating the top candidates in the lab.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our AI model, AMPs-Net, outperformed existing methods by a significant margin. Using our pipeline, we identified two previously unreported antimicrobial motifs and a novel multifunctional peptide with therapeutic potential. This work validates an AI-driven approach that makes the rational discovery of new antimicrobial drugs dramatically more efficient.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: The rise of antibiotic resistance is a critical public health threat. Discovering new antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) is a promising solution, but traditional lab-based screening is incredibly slow, costly, and inefficient, with most candidates failing.

title: Translocating Peptides of Biomedical Interest Obtained from the Spike (S) Glycoprotein of the SARS-CoV-2

laymanSummary.question: What was the outcome?
laymanSummary.answer: One of the peptides, named AHB-1, proved to be a remarkably effective cell-penetrating agent. Nanoparticles carrying AHB-1 safely and efficiently entered cells and escaped internal traps. This work demonstrates that we can learn from viruses to design better drug delivery systems, leading to more effective and targeted therapies.

title: Buforin II-Escherichia coli's DNA interactome: Detailed biophysical characterization revealed nanoscale complexes likely formed by DNA supercoiling

laymanSummary.question: What is the potential impact?
laymanSummary.answer: This work reveals that Buforin II induces DNA supercoiling, forming distinct nanoscale structures. Understanding this interaction mechanism not only clarifies its potent antimicrobial activity but also provides a blueprint for designing novel peptide-DNA complexes for applications like gene delivery vehicles.

laymanSummary.question: What was our proposed solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We performed a detailed biophysical analysis using magnetic nanobioconjugates to isolate and study the E. coli DNA fragments that interact with Buforin II. We combined advanced microscopy, spectroscopy, and genomic sequencing techniques to visualize and characterize the resulting complexes.

laymanSummary.question: What was the problem?
laymanSummary.answer: Growing antibiotic resistance is a serious global health threat. Antimicrobial peptides like Buforin II are promising alternatives, but how they interact with bacterial DNA to cause cell death is not fully understood, limiting their optimization and use.

title: Mercadeo sensorial para una vida más saludable

laymanSummary.question: What evidence is presented?
laymanSummary.answer: We present the results of two scientific experiments. The first experiment identified that the sound of a beer being poured from a bottle generates more positive emotional and sensory expectations than other sounds. The second experiment showed that when this sound accompanied an image of non-alcoholic beer, it significantly counteracted the negative perception associated with the product.

laymanSummary.question: What is the core argument?
laymanSummary.answer: The core argument is that experiential sounds, such as a beer being poured, can positively influence the negative expectations associated with non-alcoholic beer. This can be used to improve the digital shopping experience and encourage healthier consumption habits.

laymanSummary.question: Why is this important?
laymanSummary.answer: This is important because it shows how brands can use sensory elements like sound to overcome negative predispositions toward products during an e-commerce experience. It highlights that brands still focusing only on visual elements in the digital experience are falling behind, and that sound plays a critical role in customer experience.

title: Novel antibacterial hydrogels based on gelatin/polyvinyl-alcohol and graphene oxide/silver nanoconjugates: formulation, characterization, and preliminary biocompatibility evaluation

laymanSummary.question: What was our innovative solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We developed a new topical hydrogel—a soft, water-based gel—to fight skin infections. Its key antibacterial ingredient is a specially designed nanocomposite made of tiny, germ-killing silver nanoparticles attached to sheets of graphene oxide, all embedded within a biocompatible gel network.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: With antibiotic resistance on the rise, common skin infections are becoming harder to treat, creating an urgent need for new antibacterial solutions that are effective, safe, and easy to apply.

laymanSummary.question: What were the results?
laymanSummary.answer: The hydrogel was highly effective, completely inhibiting the growth of widespread bacteria like E. coli and S. aureus in lab tests. Crucially, it also proved to be safe and biocompatible, with minimal impact on human cells and blood. This study demonstrates a powerful new platform for treating skin infections that could serve as an effective alternative to conventional antibiotics.

title: Novel Developments on Stimuli-Responsive Probiotic Encapsulates: From Smart Hydrogels to Nanostructured Platforms

laymanSummary.question: What hurdles remain?
laymanSummary.answer: While these smart encapsulation techniques show great promise, key challenges remain. A major hurdle is ensuring the released probiotics can successfully establish themselves in the gut. Future research will focus on translating these innovative lab concepts into affordable, mass-produced products that can reach the market.

title: Iduronate-2-sulfatase interactome: validation by yeast two-hybrid assay

laymanSummary.question: What were the key findings?
laymanSummary.answer: We successfully confirmed that the IDS enzyme directly binds to two specific proteins: LSAMP and SYT1. These interactions are likely crucial for transporting the enzyme within cells and helping it cross the blood-brain barrier. These findings open up new avenues for understanding Hunter syndrome and could lead to innovative therapies designed to deliver the missing enzyme to the brain.

title: Multiscale Approach to Dairy Products Design

laymanSummary.question: Why is this approach important?
laymanSummary.answer: Traditional food design often focuses on just one or two scales, missing crucial connections. By understanding the entire chain of events from molecules to mouthfeel, food scientists can move beyond simple trial-and-error to intentionally design new and improved products.

laymanSummary.question: What are the potential applications?
laymanSummary.answer: This integrated strategy allows for the rational design of novel dairy products, such as healthier versions with less salt or fat, without sacrificing the texture, creaminess, and sensory qualities that consumers love and expect.

title: Engineering a heterologously expressed fructosyltransferase from Aspergillus oryzae N74 in Komagataella phaffii (Pichia pastoris) for kestose production

laymanSummary.question: What was our protein engineering solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We used a combination of computer modeling and genetic engineering to improve the enzyme responsible for production. By making targeted, single-point mutations based on predictive models, we created several new versions of the enzyme and tested their ability to selectively produce GF₂.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: 1-kestotriose (GF₂) is a highly beneficial prebiotic fiber that promotes gut health. However, the enzymes used to produce it typically create an unwanted mixture of different fiber types, making it difficult to obtain a high concentration of the target molecule.

title: Introductory Chapter: From BioBricks to Synthetic Genomes
publicationVenue: In: Synthetic Genomics: From BioBricks to Synthetic Genomes, IntechOpen

title: Synthetic Genomics: From BioBricks to Synthetic Genomes
Microfluidic Synthesis and Purification of Magnetoliposomes for Potential Applications in the Gastrointestinal Delivery of Difficult-to-Transport Drugs

laymanSummary.question: What were the results?
laymanSummary.answer: The platform was highly successful. The synthesis method achieved up to 90% drug encapsulation efficiency, and the resulting magnetoliposomes were proven to be remarkably safe and biocompatible. This work showcases a powerful new platform for developing oral medications for drugs that are otherwise difficult for the body to absorb.

title: Preparation and Characterization of an Injectable and Photo-Responsive Chitosan Methacrylate/Graphene Oxide Hydrogel: Potential Applications in Bone Tissue Adhesion and Repair

laymanSummary.question: What was our innovative solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We developed an advanced bioadhesive hydrogel made from chitosan and reinforced with graphene oxide. This gel is injectable, allowing a surgeon to apply it directly to a fracture, and can be instantly hardened in place with a blue light, avoiding the damaging heat of traditional cements.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Repairing complex bone fractures often requires implants or cements that have significant drawbacks, including poor adhesion, heat damage to tissues, and potential need for a second surgery. This creates a need for a safer, stronger, and more versatile bone adhesive.

title: Highly Efficient Synthesis of Type B Gelatin and Low Molecular Weight Chitosan Nanoparticles: Potential Applications as Bioactive Molecule Carriers and Cell-Penetrating Agents

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Nanoparticles made from natural polymers like gelatin and chitosan are excellent for delivering drugs and nutrients. However, traditional methods for creating them are often inefficient, leading to low production yields and making the process too costly for industrial scale-up.

laymanSummary.question: What was the outcome?
laymanSummary.answer: Our improved methods were a great success, achieving synthesis yields of over 90% for both gelatin and chitosan nanoparticles—a significant improvement over previous techniques. The resulting nanoparticles were also confirmed to be safe and biocompatible, paving the way for their broader application in drug delivery systems and functional foods.

laymanSummary.question: What was our improved method?
laymanSummary.answer: We developed a highly efficient and low-cost synthesis method that focuses on optimizing not just the creation of nanoparticles but also their recovery. By replacing standard centrifugation with a combination of dialysis and freeze-drying, we significantly improved the purification step and minimized product loss.

title: Design and Manufacture of a Low-Cost Microfluidic System for the Synthesis of Giant Liposomes for the Encapsulation of Yeast Homologues: Applications in the Screening of Membrane-Active Peptide Libraries
Pinched flow fractionation for size-based separation of polydisperse polymeric microparticles via a low-cost microfluidic device
publicationVenue: 2021 IEEE 2nd International Congress of Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering (CI-IB&BI)

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Separating polymeric microparticles by size is crucial for applications like drug delivery, but controlling their size during synthesis is difficult, leading to mixed (polydisperse) batches. This creates a need for an efficient and low-cost separation method.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our device successfully sorted microparticles ranging from 1 to 20 µm with high precision. This work provides an accessible and effective tool to overcome the challenge of polydispersity, which is crucial for advancing drug delivery systems and other biomedical applications.

title: Promoting Healthier Drinking Habits: Using Sound to Encourage the Choice for Non-Alcoholic Beers in E-Commerce

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Non-alcoholic beers (NABs) are a healthier alternative to traditional beer, but consumers often perceive them negatively, associating them with poor taste. We wanted to find a way to make NABs more appealing in online shopping environments.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: We discovered that a beer bottle pouring sound significantly reduced negative feelings and increased expectations of refreshment for the NAB. This finding shows that brands can strategically use sound in e-commerce to nudge consumers toward healthier choices by making those products more sensorially attractive.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We investigated whether sound could change consumer perceptions. In two experiments, we paired images of NABs with different beer-related sounds—like a can opening or a bottle pouring—and measured how these sounds affected participants' emotions and sensory expectations.

title: Microfluidics for Multiphase Mixing and Liposomal Encapsulation of Nanobioconjugates: Passive vs. Acoustic Systems
Understanding the Potential of Genome Editing in Parkinson’s Disease

title: Study of the spike (S) glycoprotein from the SARS-CoV-2 as a possible source of translocating peptides of biomedical interest
publicationVenue: ACS Fall 2021 Meeting, American Chemical Society

laymanSummary.question: What was our proposed solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We analyzed the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 to identify peptide sequences with membrane-crossing abilities. Using computer simulations, we tested how these peptides interact with cell membranes and measured the energy required for them to penetrate.

laymanSummary.question: What was the problem?
laymanSummary.answer: Getting therapeutic molecules into cells is extremely difficult because cell membranes act as barriers. We hypothesized that the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which efficiently enters human cells, might contain peptide sequences that could be repurposed as drug delivery tools.

laymanSummary.question: What is the potential impact?
laymanSummary.answer: We discovered viral peptides that perform as well as known cell-penetrating peptides. This could lead to new drug delivery systems that help medicines reach their targets inside cells more effectively, improving treatments for various diseases.

title: Gelatin-Graphene Oxide Nanocomposite Hydrogels for Kluyveromyces lactis Encapsulation: Potential Applications in Probiotics and Bioreactor Packings
Delivery Systems for Nucleic Acids and Proteins: Barriers, Cell Capture Pathways and Nanocarriers

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: This review provides a foundational understanding of the complex interactions between nanocarriers and biological environments. By consolidating the current knowledge on delivery challenges and solutions, our work helps guide the rational design of the next generation of nanovehicles, aiming to accelerate the clinical translation of advanced gene and protein therapies.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We conducted a comprehensive review of non-viral delivery systems, focusing on various types of nanocarriers. We detailed the biological barriers these systems must overcome, the cellular mechanisms for their uptake, and the diverse strategies (e.g., lipid, polymer, and inorganic nanoparticles) used to create effective vehicles for delivering nucleic acids and proteins.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Delivering therapeutic molecules like genes and proteins into target cells is a major hurdle in medicine. Biological systems have numerous extracellular and intracellular barriers that block or degrade these therapies, and traditional viral delivery methods have safety concerns. There is a critical need for safe and effective non-viral delivery systems.

title: Optimization of glycerol consumption in wild-type Escherichia coli using central carbon modeling as an alternative approach

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: The biofuel industry generates large amounts of glycerol as a by-product, reducing its competitiveness. Finding the best culture medium to enable microorganisms like E. coli to convert this glycerol into valuable products is typically a slow, tedious, and expensive trial-and-error process.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our computationally designed culture medium resulted in a two-fold increase in glycerol consumption compared to a standard lab medium. This work demonstrates that computational modeling can significantly speed up the optimization of bioprocesses, making the conversion of industrial by-products into valuable chemicals faster and more cost-effective.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We used a computational, genome-scale model to predict the ideal nutritional conditions for E. coli to consume glycerol efficiently. Our model identified that the availability of nitrogen, phosphorus, and oxygen was crucial. Based on these computational results, we designed and tested a new culture medium in the lab.

title: Modernizing the chemical engineering curriculum via a student-centered framework that promotes technical, professional, and technology expertise skills: The case of unit operations
publicationVenue: Education for Chemical Engineers, Volume 35, Pages 8-21

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We completely redesigned the course using a student-centered framework. We combined a 'flipped classroom' model (where students review material before class) with project-based learning and interactive e-learning tools to actively engage students in developing all three critical skill sets.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our intervention significantly improved students' perception of their own development in teamwork and other professional skills. The new framework created a more effective learning environment, showing that modern pedagogical approaches can better prepare engineering students for the complex demands of their future careers.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Modern engineering jobs require a mix of technical, professional, and technological skills that traditional lecture-based courses often fail to develop. We observed that our core Unit Operations course was perceived as overly demanding, causing students to struggle or delay taking it.

title: Application of a Multiscale Approach in the Substitution and Reduction of NaCl in Costeño-Type Artisan Cheese

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Costeño-type cheese, a traditional Colombian cheese, is known for its very high salt (NaCl) content. Reducing this salt for health reasons is difficult because it fundamentally changes the cheese's unique hard and crumbly texture, which consumers expect.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: We found that increasing the cooking temperature was key. This modification allowed us to significantly reduce the NaCl content while producing a cheese with a texture and physicochemical profile very similar to the traditional, high-salt version. This provides a clear, effective strategy for creating healthier food products without compromising their defining characteristics.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We took a multiscale approach, analyzing how process changes affect both microscopic structure and macroscopic texture. We experimented with reducing salt, substituting some with potassium chloride (KCl), and increasing the cooking temperature during cheesemaking.

Design, Screening, and Testing of Non-Rational Peptide Libraries with Antimicrobial Activity: In Silico and Experimental Approaches

laymanSummary.question: Summary
laymanSummary.answer: The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is a major global health threat, pushing scientists to find new ways to fight infections. One promising alternative is antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), which are small proteins naturally produced by many organisms to defend against microbes. The challenge is that finding new, effective AMPs can be like looking for a needle in a haystack. This article reviews a modern, high-tech approach to speed up this discovery process. The authors describe a workflow that combines four key technologies. First, they use artificial intelligence (specifically, deep learning) to scan huge databases of potential peptide sequences and predict which ones might have antimicrobial properties. Next, the most promising candidates are tested in a virtual environment using molecular dynamics, which are computer simulations that show how the peptide might interact with and destroy a bacterial cell membrane. The peptides that pass this virtual test are then produced in the lab by genetically engineering microorganisms to display them on their surface. Finally, these microorganisms are screened using microfluidics—tiny devices that can handle thousands of individual cells in microscopic droplets—to rapidly identify which peptides have the strongest microbe-killing abilities. This integrated, multi-stage process aims to make the search for new antimicrobial drugs faster, cheaper, and more efficient.

title: Delivery of Linear Gene-Editing Systems by Cell-Penetrating Magnetite Vehicles: Synthesis, Characterization and Preliminary In Vitro Testing

This design helps the nanoparticles enter cells and escape the internal traps. We used a fluorescent tag to track their journey and confirm their successful delivery and cargo release inside the cells.

title: Design and FEM simulation of an asymmetric pinched flow fractionation microfluidic system for high-throughput screening applications

This work validates the design and provides a clear path to manufacturing a low-cost version of this chip, which could significantly accelerate high-throughput screening and other biomedical applications.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Screening millions of potential drug candidates, like translocating peptides, is slow and expensive. A key step is separating active molecules from inactive ones, but this requires a high-throughput system that can handle microscopic components efficiently.

title: Formulation and characterization of gelatin-based hydrogels for the encapsulation of Kluyveromyces lactis and chitosan nanoparticles: biotech and biomedical applications

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Protecting delicate probiotics and therapeutic drugs as they pass through the harsh environment of the digestive system is a major challenge. This study aimed to develop a low-cost, effective encapsulation system to improve their survival and delivery.

title: In Silico Analysis of Microfluidic Systems for the Purification of Magnetoliposomes

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?

title: Modeling and Simulation of Multiphase Flow for Nanoparticle Translocation

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: To develop reproducible and optimized methods for encapsulating therapeutic magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) inside liposomes for advanced drug delivery, a process that is difficult to control with traditional techniques.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: The simulation successfully modeled the saturation kinetics observed in experiments. This provides a powerful predictive tool to refine and optimize the design of microfluidic systems for creating these nanomedicines, reducing the need for costly and time-consuming trial-and-error in the lab.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We developed an in silico (computer simulation) model to predict the performance of microfluidic devices designed for this encapsulation process. Using COMSOL Multiphysics, we simulated the flow and interaction of MNPs and liposomes, even using a chemical reaction model as an analogy to predict their binding kinetics.

title: Synthesis and characterization of a fullerenol derivative for the development of cell penetration vehicles

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Creating effective drug delivery vehicles that can bypass cellular defenses is a major challenge. Fullerenols, a type of carbon nanostructure, are promising candidates, but they must be correctly synthesized and functionalized for this purpose.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: The research successfully synthesized and characterized the fullerenol derivative, preparing it for the next stage of development. The plan is to attach potent cell-penetrating agents (like Buforin II and OmpA) to test if this new nanocarrier can improve drug delivery performance, building on previous work with other types of nanoparticles.

title: Synthesis, Characterization, and Functionalization of Chitosan and Gelatin Type B Nanoparticles to Develop Novel Highly Biocompatible Cell-Penetrating Agents

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: The research successfully created and characterized these novel nanocarriers. Initial results confirmed their desired properties, laying the groundwork for further testing to validate them as highly biocompatible and effective agents for targeted drug delivery, which could lead to safer and more potent therapies.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Developing safe and effective drug delivery vehicles that can penetrate cells and avoid being trapped and destroyed in cellular compartments called endosomes.

title: Synthesis, Characterization, and Functionalization of Graphene Oxide-Based Nanoplatforms for Gene Delivery

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Gene therapy requires delivery systems that can not only enter cells but also escape internal traps called endosomes. This study aimed to develop a new nanoplatform to overcome this critical barrier.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We proposed a novel nanocarrier by combining graphene oxide (GO) with a potent cell-penetrating peptide, Buforin II. This work focused on the crucial first step: preparing the GO and chemically modifying its surface to allow for the attachment of the peptide.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: We successfully prepared and functionalized the graphene oxide, confirmed by advanced characterization techniques. This foundational work establishes a new route for creating versatile GO-based nanoplatforms that could significantly improve the stability and effectiveness of gene delivery systems.

title: Improving employability skills through non-placement work-integrated learning in chemical and food engineering: A case study

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: There is often a gap between the skills engineering students learn at university and the practical, 'soft skills' like teamwork and creativity that industry demands. While traditional internships help, they can be difficult to secure for all students and vary in quality.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our findings show this model was highly effective at building the desired employability skills and fostering a professional identity in students. The direct interaction with industry partners was highly motivating and provided a valuable transition between academic learning and the professional workplace.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We designed and evaluated a university course where student teams solved real-world challenges provided directly by industry partners. This 'non-placement' approach gave students authentic work experience within a structured academic setting, using a problem-solving framework to guide their projects.

CFD and Experimental Characterization of a Bioreactor: Analysis via Power Curve, Flow Patterns and kLa

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Mixing operations in bioreactors are critical for growing microorganisms, but they are difficult to control and scale up. The choice of impeller and agitation speed directly affects oxygen supply, power consumption, and physical stress on the cells. We needed a systematic way to characterize these factors to find the most efficient operating conditions.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We combined physical experiments with advanced computer simulations (Computational Fluid Dynamics or CFD) to characterize a bench-top bioreactor. We tested various impeller types (Rushton, paddles, propeller) and operating conditions to measure key performance metrics like the oxygen transfer coefficient ($k_{L}a$), power consumption, and fluid flow patterns.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our study provides a detailed guide for selecting the optimal impeller configuration for different bioprocesses. We demonstrated that factors like impeller diameter can significantly reduce energy consumption and shear stress on cells without sacrificing oxygen transfer. This work provides a reliable and affordable methodology to ensure proper mixing and oxygen availability, which directly improves cell growth, yield, and overall productivity in industrial biotechnology.

title: pH-Responsive, Cell-Penetrating, Core/Shell Magnetite/Silver Nanoparticles for the Delivery of Plasmids: Preparation, Characterization, and Preliminary In Vitro Evaluation

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our nanovehicle was shown to be highly biocompatible, with minimal toxicity to human cells. It successfully loaded plasmid DNA and demonstrated a remarkable ability to enter cells and escape the internal compartments that typically degrade foreign material. This design provides a promising and safe platform to improve the efficiency of future gene therapies.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Gene therapies, like CRISPR, hold immense promise but face a major delivery problem: getting the therapeutic genetic material safely inside the target cells. We need a vehicle that can protect its cargo, penetrate cell defenses, and release the genes only once inside, all without harming the patient.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We engineered a multi-stage smart nanoparticle. It features a magnetic core with a silver shell, which we coated with a pH-responsive polymer. This polymer holds onto DNA in the bloodstream but releases it in the acidic environment inside a cell. We also added a cell-penetrating peptide, Buforin II, to help it efficiently cross the cell membrane.

title: Lysosomal storage diseases: current therapies and future alternatives

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our review synthesizes the progress and challenges in treating LSDs, highlighting that genome editing offers a revolutionary path toward potentially curative therapies. By outlining the state-of-the-art and future directions, we provide a critical resource for researchers aiming to develop more effective treatments that can address the full spectrum of symptoms, including the difficult-to-treat neurological aspects of these diseases.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We conducted a comprehensive review of the current therapeutic landscape for LSDs. We analyzed established methods like enzyme replacement therapy and substrate reduction therapy, and then provided a detailed overview of cutting-edge alternatives, with a special focus on genome editing technologies like CRISPR/Cas9.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Lysosomal storage diseases (LSDs) are a group of serious genetic disorders caused by the buildup of harmful substances in cells. Current treatments, like enzyme replacement therapy, are not always effective and struggle to treat the neurological damage associated with many of these conditions.

title: Formulation and Characterization of Gelatin-Based Hydrogels for the Encapsulation of Kluyveromyces lactis-Applications in Packed-Bed Reactors and Probiotics Delivery in Humans

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We proposed to encapsulate the probiotic yeast Kluyveromyces lactis on chemically crosslinked gelatin hydrogels. We performed a comprehensive characterization of the hydrogels to identify critical parameters that facilitate encapsulation and enhance cell survival.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our results showed that the selected hydrogels led to cell viability levels approaching 95% in bioreactor operations and 50% in simulated GI tract media. These results indicate that the proposed encapsulates are suitable to overcome major issues of oral administration of probiotics and open the possibility for further biotech applications.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: One of the main issues when orally administering microorganism-based probiotics is the significant loss of bioactivity as they pass through the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. A cost-effective method was needed to protect them.

title: Demulsification of Colombian Heavy Crude Oil (W/O) Emulsions: Insights into the Instability Mechanisms, Chemical Structure, and Performance of Different Commercial Demulsifiers

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: Our results showed that for heavy crude, strong interfacial activity is not the most important factor. The most effective demulsifiers were those that also intermingled with the oil phase to slightly increase the density difference between the oil and water. This small density change provides the critical driving force for separation. This insight provides a new, crucial design principle for developing next-generation demulsifiers tailored for the growing market of heavy and unconventional oils.

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We developed an enhanced method to evaluate demulsifiers by combining traditional "bottle tests" with advanced optical measurements (transmission/backscattering) for a real-time, quantitative look at emulsion breakdown. We applied this method to a Colombian heavy crude oil, testing a wide range of commercial demulsifiers and correlating their performance with changes in interfacial properties and their chemical structure, which we analyzed via HPLC-MS.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Heavy crude oil is often extracted with water, creating extremely stable water-in-oil emulsions. The chemicals used to separate water from light oil (demulsifiers) are ineffective on these heavy crudes, and the scientific reasons for this failure are not well understood, making it difficult to select or design better alternatives.

title: Design and Manufacture of Novel Airlift Milibioreactors: A Low-Cost Lab Scale Approach for Proof-of-Concept Experiments
publicationVenue: 2019 AIChE Annual Meeting, Session: Advances in Bioprocess Design for Cell Culture and Bioproduct Production

laymanSummary.answer: Our Milibioreactors provide an affordable alternative for bioprocess research, enabling more laboratories to conduct optimization experiments. By reducing costs and volumes while maintaining functionality, we can accelerate the development of biotechnology applications and make bioprocess research more accessible.

laymanSummary.question: What was the problem?
laymanSummary.answer: Commercially available bioreactors for scaling up bioprocesses are expensive, require large volumes, and have complex assembly procedures. This makes it difficult for researchers to conduct affordable proof-of-concept experiments, especially when testing delicate cell cultures that need precise conditions.

laymanSummary.question: What was our proposed solution?
laymanSummary.answer: We designed and manufactured 200 mL "Milibioreactors" - miniaturized airlift bioreactors that can be produced using low-cost 3D printing and molding techniques. These systems feature external loops for gentle mixing, integrated sensors for monitoring, and customizable designs for different experimental needs.

laymanSummary.answer: This solution enables sustainable pig farming while protecting the forest reserve ecosystem. The community gains economic benefits from waste-derived products, reduces environmental fines, and serves as a model for other rural communities facing similar waste management challenges in cold climates.

laymanSummary.answer: Breweries generate large amounts of yeast waste that contains valuable compounds like β-glucan, a bioactive molecule with health benefits. This waste is typically discarded, missing opportunities for creating high-value products.

title: Identification of the iduronate-2-sulfatase proteome in wild-type mouse brain

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We used proteomic and neurochemical methods on wild-type mouse brains to create a comprehensive interaction map for IDS. Using the IDS enzyme as bait, we performed affinity purification to capture its binding partners, which we then identified using mass spectrometry. We validated these interactions with bioinformatics tools and co-immunoprecipitation assays.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: We successfully identified 187 potential protein partners for IDS, creating the first "social network" for this enzyme in the brain. This revealed that IDS is involved in a much broader range of functions than previously thought, including cell structure, transport, and redox balance. This work provides a rich dataset of new targets for understanding the pathology of Mucopolysaccharidosis II and for developing novel therapeutic strategies.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: The enzyme Iduronate-2-sulfatase (IDS) is critical for cellular waste disposal, and its deficiency causes the severe neurological disorder Mucopolysaccharidosis II. While its main role was known, we lacked a map of its protein interactions in the brain, limiting our understanding of its full function and the disease's complexity.

title: Applying PBL methodologies to the chemical engineering courses: Unit operations and modeling and simulation, using a joint course project

laymanSummary.question: What was our approach?
laymanSummary.answer: We redesigned the courses using a Project-Based Learning (PBL) methodology, centered around a joint project. Students worked in teams to design, 3D print, and experimentally test a centrifugal pump, while also modeling its performance using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations.

laymanSummary.question: What was the challenge?
laymanSummary.answer: Students in chemical engineering often perceive core subjects like 'Unit Operations' and 'Modeling and Simulation' as separate fields, struggling to integrate them to solve real-world problems. This separation also contributed to an excessive academic workload.

laymanSummary.question: What was the impact?
laymanSummary.answer: The new methodology successfully reduced the students' perceived workload by about 25%. Student feedback was overwhelmingly positive, with 85% confirming that the hands-on, integrated project benefited their learning process. This approach effectively connected abstract theories to tangible applications, fostering a deeper, more integrated understanding of the subjects.

laymanSummary.answer: We designed an aptamer (a short RNA molecule) using computer simulations that changes its shape when it encounters isoflavones.
